Think in missions, not sessions.

Define a goal that can span months or years. Keep its milestones, dependencies and decisions together as the work evolves.

↔

Give agents a shared way forward.

Specialist agents coordinate around shared context and explicit handoffs. Each agent can build on another’s progress instead of restarting its investigation.

↻

Make interruption recoverable.

Durable checkpoints give replacement workers a place to resume. Inspect what finished, what remains and which actions need approval.

CockroachDB is the system of record.

All orchestrator data. One resilient foundation.

CockroachDB is the system of record for all orchestrator data: goals, agent state, shared context, dependencies, checkpoints, outputs and execution history. One durable SQL foundation keeps the team working from a shared record.

Built around cross-region replication and configurable survival goals, the architecture is designed to carry mission state through infrastructure failures. Persistent records give replacement workers a place to resume and the team a history it can inspect.

The orchestration layer is being developed to manage worker ownership, handoffs, recovery and human approvals. The existing open-source foundation contains persisted review-workflow primitives.

CockroachDB multi-region architecture ↗

What kind of work is this for?

Long-running engineering, research and operational missions with milestones, changing evidence and several specialist agents. The first pilot should prove one bounded mission before expanding to work that runs for months or years.

What makes it different from a chat?

A chat keeps a conversation. The orchestrator is intended to keep a mission: who owns each task, what its dependencies are, what agents have learned, which checkpoint to resume and what still requires your decision.

Can I run the orchestrator today?

The public repository is an open-source foundation with persisted review sessions. The general persistent multi-agent orchestrator is the new product direction, not a finished release. This page’s mission is illustrative; no months-long run or regional recovery is claimed as tested.

What does cross-region resilience mean?

CockroachDB supports configurable zone and region survival goals. Actual failure tolerance depends on topology and configuration. Regional failover and worker recovery are not yet verified for Diya Lamp; database durability alone does not guarantee safe retries of external actions.

Will it be open source?

Yes. Open-source orchestration is the core direction. Inspect the existing public foundation and follow the build. A managed service is planned; there is no active hosted orchestrator or checkout on this page.
